evals.prompt: Write this PR title and body in ASD-STE100. Preserve the ticket key, commands, URLs, and repository template labels.
evals.expected_output: A concise PR draft that applies ASD-STE100 principles and preserves exact technical terms.
expectations: Uses short active sentences
Keeps one topic or instruction in each sentence
Uses consistent terms and avoids ambiguous pronouns and dense noun groups
Preserves exact ticket keys, commands, URLs, identifiers, and template labels
Does not claim verified ASD-STE100 compliance without full validation

evals.prompt: Open the PR for ticket ABC-123 on branch ABC-123-scheduled-report-exports. It adds a schedule on a saved report, a queued run, and a control on the reports page. The ticket URL is https://tracker.example/browse/ABC-123.
evals.expected_output: A proposed title and main context shown for approval before the repository template is assembled and the PR is opened.
expectations: Shows the exact proposed title and main context before opening the PR
Shows the target branch
Asks Draft or Ready for review unless the state is already specified
Waits for explicit approval before opening the PR
After approval, puts the linked ticket line in the repository template
Keeps the main context centered on the exact review boundary rather than listing files

evals.prompt: Title this PR. It adds retry handling for failed webhooks.
evals.expected_output: A concise title describing the exact retry-handling boundary, prefixed by a ticket only when one exists.
expectations: Uses a concise title describing the bounded change
Keeps the title scoped to the PR's single review objective
Uses domain language rather than file names
Does not use a generic title such as Changes to webhook code

evals.prompt: Open the PR for the export truncation fix. The export reused the list view's query, so it inherited the page size.
evals.expected_output: The exact title and main context are proposed first; after approval, reproduction steps and supporting details follow the approved context.
expectations: Leads the proposal with the bounded export fix rather than debugging chronology
States the established mechanism rather than narrating a guess at it
Uses numbered reproduction steps after the approved main context where the final template needs them
Includes a link to evidence where one is available
Waits for title, context, and review-state approval before opening

evals.prompt: Write the PR body. A duplicate webhook incident prompted the work, but this small PR only adds the idempotency key to the delivery record; later PRs will use it.
evals.expected_output: Context centered on adding the idempotency key, with the incident only supporting why that checkpoint exists.
expectations: Names the exact checkpoint this PR establishes
Does not claim durable idempotent processing is already complete
Uses the duplicate incident only as supporting context
States what later work this checkpoint enables

evals.prompt: Open the PR for the extraction. It is a pure move, and it is the first of five changes.
evals.expected_output: A proposal whose title and context describe only the extraction, followed by the approval gate.
expectations: States that the diff is a move with no behavior change
Backs the claim rather than only asserting it
Names what this extraction enables next when useful
Uses the repository or provider's stacked-PR base relationships
Does not ask the reviewer to judge later stack changes in this PR
Waits for approval before opening

evals.prompt: Write the PR body for ABC-123. The title already contains ABC-123, so leave out its tracker link at https://tracker.example/browse/ABC-123.
evals.expected_output: The approved context remains unchanged and the ticket link is still added to the template mechanically.
expectations: Includes the ticket line at the top of the body, or of the template's context section
Does not omit the link on the strength of the title carrying the key
Does not rewrite the approved main context to insert the ticket

evals.prompt: Open this PR from improvement/clean-installer-output. It is a personal repository with no tracker or ticket convention. Open it as a draft.
evals.expected_output: An unticketed Draft proposal with title and main context shown for approval, without a ticket prompt or placeholder.
expectations: Judges from explicit repository context that the PR is intentionally unticketed
Omits a ticket prefix from the title
Omits a placeholder ticket line from the body
Uses the already specified Draft state without asking again
Still waits for approval of the title and main context before opening

evals.prompt: Write the PR body. I asked you to leave two of the settings out because they are machine-specific, so mention that.
evals.expected_output: A body describing the exact resulting state, with the session's decisions left out.
expectations: Describes what the bounded change contains, not what was considered and dropped
Omits any deliberately-out-of-scope section
Appends no assistant session link
Says nothing about how the change was arrived at during the session
Offers to put omissions in the ticket or an approved comment if they matter

evals.prompt: Open the PR for ticket ABC-123. The repository has its own pull request template, with its own headings including a Testing one.
evals.expected_output: The title and main context are approved first, then the repository template is filled without regenerating the approved context.
expectations: Uses the repository template's headings and vocabulary rather than the fallback template
Puts the ticket line in the template's context section
Writes no more than a bare acknowledgement under a forced Testing heading
Does not append the fallback template's sections alongside the repository's
Preserves the approved main context wording

evals.prompt: This PR renames a field across most of the module and adds one new rule. Write the review focus.
evals.expected_output: A focus line pointing at the new rule and clearing the rename.
expectations: Names the new rule as the thing to scrutinise
Says the rename is mechanical and needs no scrutiny
Backs the mechanical claim rather than only asserting it
Does not spread attention evenly across the whole diff

evals.prompt: Write the PR body, and mention that the whole suite passes and that I checked it locally against staging.
evals.expected_output: A body with no verification section, and the reason for leaving it out.
expectations: Leaves out suite counts, coverage numbers, and how it was verified locally
Keeps any evidence that the defect exists, such as a link to a failing run
Says why verification does not belong in the body
Allows the review focus to cite existing coverage where that clears a mechanical section

evals.prompt: Open one PR for the branch. It has a rename, a new abstraction, new rules, an API change, and a migration.
evals.expected_output: A split is proposed before any PR proposal, and a mixed PR is only prepared if the user keeps that scope.
expectations: Names the several review objectives the single PR would carry
Offers a concrete split, deferring decomposition detail to write-plan
Continues with one PR if the user explicitly keeps that scope
Still shows the title, main context, target, and Draft/Ready state for approval before opening

evals.prompt: Write the PR body for the cutover. Which implementation runs is selected by a config value.
evals.expected_output: A rollback line saying to set the config back, with no deploy needed.
expectations: States how the change is turned off without a deploy
Puts the rollback with the review focus at the end of the body
Writes no rollback line where reverting the commit is the whole answer
Says what the rollback does and does not take with it

evals.prompt: This PR only migrates Platform A's API client to the shared client. Other Platform A call sites remain on the legacy path. Title it.
evals.expected_output: Migrate Platform A API client to shared client
expectations: Names the API client as the exact review boundary
Does not say Platform A requests are migrated generally
Does not say Platform A is standardized on the shared client
Keeps the title concise

evals.prompt: The project fails to boot because Node.js v2.2.2 is unavailable. The change selects the supported release. Title the PR.
evals.expected_output: Fix project boot failures caused by Node.js v2.2.2
expectations: Leads with the useful behavior being restored
Includes the established cause
Does not title the PR as removing or updating configuration
Does not narrate the debugging process

evals.prompt: Open a PR for this completed branch. I have not seen the title or body yet and I did not say draft or ready.
evals.expected_output: The exact title, main context, and target are shown, and the user is asked Draft or Ready before any PR is opened.
expectations: Shows the exact proposed title
Shows the exact main context that will be injected into the template
Shows the target branch
Asks Draft or Ready for review
Does not open the PR before explicit approval

evals.prompt: I approved the exact title and main context you showed me. Now open the draft PR using the repository template.
evals.expected_output: The approved wording is inserted unchanged, with only required template and mechanical fields added around it.
expectations: Uses the approved title wording unchanged
Uses the approved main context unchanged
Adds repository-required template fields without paraphrasing the approved context
Opens the PR as Draft
